United States (federal).unit: USD cash wages to one household employee in the calendar year
United States (federal).detail: Covers housekeepers, nannies, private teachers and in-home caregivers. Employer and employee each owe 7.65% (6.2% Social Security + 1.45% Medicare), reported on Schedule H with Form 1040.
United States (federal).note: Some older pages still show $2,800 for 2025.

United States (federal).unit: USD cash wages to all household employees in any calendar quarter
United States (federal).detail: 6% on the first $7,000 per employee, with up to a 5.4% credit for state UI.

New York.detail: Overtime at 1.5x after 40 hours a week, or after 44 hours for live-in workers. A 24-hour day of rest each week; work on it is paid at overtime if the worker agrees to work. Three paid days of rest a year after one year with the same employer.

New York.unit: USD cash wages in a calendar quarter, after which the employer is liable from the first day of that quarter

California / Los Angeles.item: City of Los Angeles minimum wage
Domestic Worker Bill of Rights (AB 241; made permanent by SB 1015)
California / Los Angeles.detail: Personal attendants (supervising, feeding or dressing a child, or an elderly or disabled person) get 1.5x over 9 hours a day or 45 hours a week. If more than 20% of a week goes on non-care chores, regular California overtime rules apply that week. Excludes family members, under-18 babysitters and casual babysitters.
$750+ cash wages in a quarter: register and withhold SDI. $1,000+ in a quarter: also pay UI and ETT.

Connecticut / New Haven.detail: Overtime at 1.5x over 40 hours in a 7-day week, but not for live-in employees. New-employer SUI rate is 1.9% on the first $27,000. A domestic worker paid $1,000+ in a 3-month period can claim UI. A Domestic Workers' Bill of Rights adds further requirements for employers of 3 or more domestic employees.

United Kingdom / London.item: Hiring a nanny or domestic worker directly
United Kingdom / London.detail: Register with HMRC as an employer and run PAYE before the first payday. A secondary source puts the trigger at paying at or above £96/week. Workplace pension auto-enrolment applies, with a 5% total minimum contribution reported.
United Kingdom / London.note: The auto-enrolment trigger was not read from a source. The HMRC rates page did not list it.

Ireland / Dublin.item: Registering as an employer of a domestic worker
Ireland / Dublin.detail: Register with Revenue if paying €40 a week or more. There is an exemption for a single domestic employee paid under €40 a week. The employer deducts PAYE, PRSI and USC and pays employer PRSI.

Ireland / Dublin.item: Code of Practice for Protecting Persons Employed in Other People's Homes
Ireland / Dublin.detail: Domestic workers have the same rights as any employee. A written statement of core terms is due within 5 days. Board and lodging deductions must be stated in the contract. From 2026-01-01 the maximum deductions are €1.27 per hour worked for meals and €33.42 a week (€4.77 a day) for accommodation only.
Income tax exemption on gross childminding income up to €15,000. PRSI still applies.

Ontario / Toronto.detail: Domestic workers get the general minimum wage. Room and board may count toward minimum wage, but only if actually received: a private room $31.70/week, meals $2.55 each up to $53.55/week, or both $85.25/week. Homemakers are exempt from hours, overtime and rest rules but are paid for at most 12 hours a day.
Ontario / Toronto.note: The room-and-board dollar figures came via a summary that may predate 2026. Verify them on the Ontario page.

Ontario / Toronto.detail: If the caregiver, babysitter or domestic worker is an employee, withhold income tax, CPP and EI and issue a T4. The employer matches CPP and pays 1.4x the employee's EI premium. If the worker is self-employed, nothing is withheld and a T4A is issued. Either party may ask CRA for a CPP/EI ruling.

British Columbia / Vancouver.note: The same increase applies to resident caretakers and live-in home-support workers.

British Columbia / Vancouver.item: Domestic workers under the BC ESA
British Columbia / Vancouver.detail: A domestic worker (cooking, cleaning or childcare who lives in the employer's private residence) must be registered with the Employment Standards Branch within 30 days of hire. A signed written contract is required (ESA s.14) covering duties, hours, wage, pay schedule and any room and board charges.

Mexico / Mexico City.note: The article does not cite the DOF directly. It conflicts with the IMSS-related reporting that uses the general minimum (315.04) as the contribution floor. Confirm against CONASAMI's DOF resolution of 2025-12-09.

Mexico / Mexico City.detail: Mandatory under the Ley del Seguro Social reform, in force since 2023-05-16 per reporting. Applies to work of more than 4 hours a day at one home on at least 3 days a week. The contribution base cannot be below the general minimum wage. Coverage includes medical care, work risks, disability, retirement savings and childcare. Registration can be done online. The fine for non-registration is MXN 2,346-41,058 (20-350 UMA, Art. 304-B LSS). About 1.8% of domestic workers are registered.

Mexico / Mexico City.item: LFT employer obligations for domestic workers
Mexico / Mexico City.detail: Aguinaldo of at least 15 days' wages by 20 December, pro-rated for a part year. Live-in workers get 9 consecutive hours of night rest, 3 hours of rest a day between shifts and 1.5 days of rest a week. Rights exist even without a written contract.

tipping_norms.gaps: No published tipping norms were found for trades (plumbers, electricians, handymen), driving instructors, music or dance teachers in any city. In the UK and Ireland, tipping tradespeople is not a published norm. No Mexico-specific guidance was found per service.
